name: Banking
description: Bank statement import and reconciliation -- the #1 practical anti-fraud control, and the one place a third party's independent record enters the system (plan/bank-import-reconciliation-spec.md). The posture is evidence handling, not ETL: bank_lines are append-only, keep their original row verbatim in `raw`, and are never hand-edited, so nobody can quietly reshape the evidence to agree with the books. Imports check THEMSELVES -- a statement carries its own checksum, so tie-out (opening + lines == closing) and continuity (this opening == the last statement's closing) run at import time and set the import's status; flagged imports still store their lines because hiding a truncated statement is exactly the failure this control catches, and the flags record which checks RAN so a balance-less CSV never reads as trustworthy as a tied-out one. Dedup is by the bank's own transaction id when the format has one (OFX FITID), else an ordinal-disambiguated content hash so genuine same-day twins both land while a re-imported file adds nothing; file-level idempotency is by sha256 of the statement itself. Reading a bank's export is DATA (bank_import_profiles.column_map), authored once with AI help and executed deterministically thereafter -- an AI that re-reads statements every month is nondeterministic and unauditable, the opposite of a control. Pure parsing/hashing/gate logic lives in object_banking.py at the repository root, a plain importable library like object_stock.py and object_finance.py, not a registered object. This slice ships the evidence layer (collections, the CSV importer, the duplicate gate); the matcher, the resolution verbs that compose journals through object_finance.compose_posted_journal, and the reconciliation statement view are the next slices of the same spec.
